items: Halogenoalkanes can be prepared by the halogenation of alkanes in the presence of light.
They can also be prepared by the electrophilic addition of hydrogen halides to alkenes.
Alcohols may be converted to the corresponding alkyl halides by the action of halogen acid in the presence of ZnCl₂ which acts as a catalyst.

Alcohols also react with thionyl chloride in pyridine as a catalyst to give alkyl chlorides. This method is especially useful since the by-products (HCl and SO₂) are gases which go off leaving behind the pure product.
Phosphorus trihalides or phosphorus pentahalides react with alcohols to replace – OH group by a halo group.

Alcohols can be converted to halogenoalkanes by reacting with potassium bromide and an acid like sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) or phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄). This method is commonly used to prepare bromoalkanes and iodoalkanes. The acid first reacts with potassium bromide to give hydrogen bromide which then further reacts with alcohols to give bromoalkanes.

blocks.text_alt: CH₃–CH₂–OH (ethanol) + KBr + H₂SO₄ → CH₃–CH₂–Br (bromoethane) + H₂O + KHSO₄

blocks.text: Phosphoric acid is preferably used to prepare iodoalkanes because it is a weak oxidizing agent and less likely to oxidize iodide ions to iodine.

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: Bromoethane is naturally emitted primarily by marine algae and phytoplankton such as trichodesmium. These organisms convert seawater bromide into volatile organobromides. Once in the atmosphere, bromoethane contributes to the global bromine cycle and plays a role in stratospheric ozone depletion.
bold: marine algae and phytoplankton such as trichodesmium

blocks.prompt: a) Give two methods to convert methanol into chloromethane.
blocks.explanation:
Any two:
CH₃OH + HCl → CH₃Cl + H₂O (ZnCl₂ catalyst)
CH₃OH + SOCl₂ → CH₃Cl + SO₂ + HCl (pyridine)
CH₃OH + PCl₅ → CH₃Cl + POCl₃ + HCl

blocks.prompt: b) Give reactions of propanol with SOCl₂ and PBr₃.
blocks.explanation:
CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + SOCl₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + SO₂ + HCl (pyridine)
3CH₃CH₂CH₂OH + PBr₃ → 3CH₃CH₂CH₂Br + H₃PO₃

blocks.prompt: c) Can we prepare fluoromethane using methane and fluorine gas?
blocks.explanation: Not in practice: fluorine reacts with methane explosively. The reaction cannot be controlled, so instead of replacing just one H by F it gives a mixture of different fluorinated products, carbon and HF.
